description: Lightweight single entrypoint for resolving Project OS behavior. Every agent resolves the kernel here before non-trivial work: this manifest owns the load order, the surface-aware resolution_strategy, and the resolution_sequence. Stable behavior lives in kernel/*.json; live project state lives only in GitHub; adapters, templates, and docs only boot agents into this manifest and shape output.

resolution_strategy.owner: This manifest is the single resolution entrypoint and owns surface-aware routing: identify the execution surface, resolve current_actor_type from actors.json, then take the matching path below. Adapters, templates, and docs point to this strategy and never define a competing resolution order. Unknown surface resolves to actor.unknown and fails closed.
resolution_strategy.terminal: Terminal surface (actor.terminal_agent) with a kernel checkout and repo-local Python: the default is the deterministic resolver fast path 'python3 -m tools.project_os_resolve --actor <actor> --workflow <workflow> --mode <mode>', which reads the current kernel JSON and expands the resolution_sequence below.
resolution_strategy.browser_and_non_terminal: Browser chat (actor.browser_chat) and every other non-terminal surface never run repo-local Python; they resolve by reading this manifest and the kernel JSON directly.
resolution_strategy.canonical_fallback: Manual resolution from this manifest and the kernel JSON is the canonical fallback for every surface and the source the fast path expands; the resolver never replaces this manifest.
resolution_strategy.non_authorization: Resolver output and manual resolution both only shape behavior and gates; neither grants permission (boundary.output_not_permission).

resolution_sequence: 1. Resolve current_actor_type from actors.json and take the matching path in resolution_strategy (terminal fast path, or manual manifest/kernel read for browser and non-terminal surfaces).
2. Load statuses.json and boundaries.json. Boundaries always apply; no later selection relaxes them.
3. Resolve execution_mode from the PM instruction for this task. Default is mode.review_only when no mode is explicitly scoped.
4. Select the workflow from workflows.json that matches the requested task.

5. Collect the evidence required by the workflow and mode from evidence.json. All issue, PR, branch, commit, review, and validation state is read live from GitHub and git, never from durable files or memory.
6. Select the output contract from outputs.json required by the workflow. Output shape never grants permission.
7. Emit exactly one status from statuses.json. When gates conflict, the stricter status wins.

source_of_truth.live_state: GitHub issues, PRs, commits, comments, reviews, branches, and local git output, read at task time
source_of_truth.adapters: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, adapters/, templates/, and docs/ point back to this manifest and never override the kernel.

size_budget.rationale: The kernel must stay cheap for agents to resolve per session. The validator fails the kernel when the hard budget is exceeded.

non_authorization: Nothing in this kernel grants write permission, write authorization, merge, closure, label, tag, release, settings, or automation authority. Permission comes only from exact scoped PM approval plus the kernel-resolved gates for the specific action.
